note: Discovery only. A Vial is a declarative .vial.json manifest hosted by its author. Osmograph installs a manifest from a raw HTTPS URL and runs the same local policy gate as a file import. A registry entry is not a security review, a safety certification, or an endorsement.

vials.name: Anomaly Watch
vials.author: @opensmell
vials.tagline: A clean baseline, a sustained change, and a decision to inspect.
vials.summary: A same-device change watch built on Osmograph's live anomaly engine: a clean baseline, a local log, alert-level rules, and a hard refusal. Not a chemical identifier, concentration meter, or safety device.
vials.install: Included in Osmograph. Open Vials → Aromatory → Anomaly Watch.

vials.name: Fermentation Lab
vials.author: @opensmell
vials.tagline: Track the batch, not just the bubble.
vials.summary: A batch log for pH, temperature, salt, visual cues, and your own array baseline, with food safety kept out of the smell channel.
vials.install: Included in Osmograph. Open Vials → Aromatory → Fermentation Lab.

vials.name: Plant Respiration
vials.author: @opensmell
vials.tagline: Watch the plant, not just the number.
vials.summary: A weekly plant-health workspace that pairs array response with light, water, leaf, and root context, and states what the array cannot see.
vials.install: Included in Osmograph. Open Vials → Aromatory → Plant Respiration.

vials.name: Coffee Roast Log
vials.author: @example-author
vials.tagline: Track the roast, not just the aroma.
vials.summary: A small example workspace for logging roast batches and the context that changes what the array response means. It is a template for authors, not a validated roasting controller.
vials.install: Paste the manifest URL into Osmograph → Vials → Aromatory → Install from URL.
